existing_source_qualifications.title: Sarah Carter, review of Adele Perry, On the Edge of Empire, BC Studies 136 (Winter 2002/03): 117–119.
existing_source_qualifications.citation: Sarah Carter, review of On the Edge of Empire: Gender, Race and the Making of British Columbia, 1849–1871, by Adele Perry, BC Studies 136 (2002/03): 117–119.

verification.note: Read in full: pp. 117 and 119 in the single-review PDF (OJS 185112, which omits p. 118) and p. 118 in the issue's book-review PDF (OJS 1654). Passages used: 'racially plural, rough and turbulent'; 'a fiction of our own invention' (Perry, p. 201); 'a settler colony where dispossesion [sic] … and resettlement … were intertwined'; 'a valuable Canadian contribution to "Whiteness" studies' (p. 117); mixed-race relationships 'not confined to the fur trade' and the 'happy stories' (Perry, p. 62) (p. 118); 'a sharp disjuncture between colonial discourse and colonial practice'; the North American setting; 'social centrality and political agency' to be 'further developed' (p. 119).

existing_source_qualifications.scope_note: In-period review by a historian of the Prairie West.
